note: Patcher matrix for B190. BUILT FROM main AT 94bcf83 (PR #350). B190 exists for ONE defect: the spa lounger orientation (#330), on its SIXTH attempt. The owner playtested B189, photographed the villager still lying ACROSS the lounger, and diagnosed it directly: flip the villager orientation horizontally for the spa receiving actions. WHY FIVE EARLIER ROUNDS COULD NOT HAVE WORKED. Every one of them argued about WHICH orientation takes WHICH strip -- northeast versus northwest -- and B189 added a handle gate so the spa rule could not reach ordinary chaises. All of that tunes a SELECTOR. The receiving pose needs the MIRROR of whatever that selector picks, so both placements were wrong together and tuning the selector could only swap which one looked wrong. The 'one lounger correct, one wrong' symptom on B188 was TWO STACKED DEFECTS: the selector wrong for one placement, on top of the mirror wrong for both. THE FIX IS SCOPED TO VF2PlanSpaTreatment, the receiving pose. SUPERSEDED BY THE OWNER'S B190 PLAYTEST -- this field originally said 'head, body and sleep strip all take the opposite arm together, so the settle and the sleep cannot disagree.' The owner then observed that BEFORE the villager closes their eyes the pose is WRONG and AFTER they close them it is RIGHT, which means the settle and the sleep strip index facing DIFFERENTLY and must NOT be coupled. Coupling them is precisely why every earlier round could correct one phase only by breaking the other. The settle and the strip now deliberately take OPPOSITE arms; see PR #352. The giving villager plans no pose at all (PlanToWork only), and the two chaise relax poses plus every ordinary and mobile Lounge Chair keep the facing the owner confirmed working. B189's handle gate is UNCHANGED and still correct; it was never the problem, it simply could not fix a defect living in the mirror. SEEDED FROM B189, so the Exercise Bike (0x99) and Ping-Pong Table (0x9a) content maps are inherited. A seed predating them would drop that art silently while the build still reported success. NOT PLAYTESTED AT BUILD TIME. 115 tests pass and three mutations are caught -- body un-mirrored, head un-mirrored, strip not mirrored -- SUPERSEDED CLAIM -- this note originally said 'no check on the artifact can verify this fix'. That was OVERSTATED and review was right to reject it: the absence of SYMBOLS does not make the mapping unobservable, because the instructions are still decodable. Measured against the shipped executable: the SleepNE/SleepNW literals are referenced 18 times in .text -- 7 as push imm32 and 11 as mov reg,imm32, so a push-only scan finds 7 and is the WRONG DENOMINATOR -- and the decode reproduces the stock CBehavior::RestingBody mapping at two independent sites (orientation 0 -> body 9 -> SleepNW; orientation 1 -> body 0x17 chaise -> SleepNE), which is known-good ground truth. What remains accurately true is NARROWER: no string, hash or file-level gate can observe this fix, and A BUILD THAT OMITTED IT WOULD PASS EVERY GATE REPORTED HERE. VF2PlanSpaTreatment is static and inlined with no prologue to anchor on, and the strip selection near its call sites compiles to a branchless cmov, so the spa mapping specifically is NOT YET CONFIRMED present in the artifact. That is an OPEN VERIFICATION GAP, recorded rather than papered over, and it is a reason to DO the binary decode, not to skip it. See docs/B190-release-notes.md, which must not be allowed to disagree with this field. Issue #330 stays open until the owner confirms both loungers in play.
